claims.text: Powder-pack boriding can form a boride surface layer on an alloy component.
Increasing boriding temperature and extending treatment duration enhance boride-layer growth kinetics.
The optimized boriding treatment will produce a thicker boride layer.
The optimized boriding treatment will produce a denser, lower-porosity boride layer.
The optimized boriding treatment will produce a more continuous and uniform boride layer.
The resulting surface layer will contain MB and M2B boride phases.
A continuous, dense MB/M2B layer acts as a barrier against penetration by molten aluminum.
A thicker and more uniform boride layer reduces aluminum diffusion into the component substrate.
Reduced aluminum diffusion minimizes chemical attack on the substrate.
The boride barrier reduces dissolution of substrate metal elements into molten aluminum.
Optimized-borided components will have lower mass loss than conventionally borided or untreated components during molten-aluminum exposure.
Optimized-borided components will corrode more slowly than conventionally borided or untreated components in molten aluminum.
Reduced molten-aluminum corrosion will extend component service life in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
Around 700°C is a typical molten-aluminum temperature for hot-dip aluminum plating.
The protective effect should remain effective around 700°C and over industrial hot-dip-plating immersion times.
Extreme temperature changes, bath-composition changes, or interactions with other bath constituents may compromise the protective effect.
